newsitem.title: USA: Alabama bill would raise school tax revenues.
newsitem.headline: Alabama bill would raise school tax revenues.

text.p: An Alabama lawmaker introduced legislation Tuesday that would require each school district to levy at least 20 mills of property tax.
Currently, school districts must levy at least 10 mills of property taxes or raise an equivalent amount of money through other means.

The bill filed by Rep. Nelson Starkey, D-Florence, would limit annual millage rate increases to 5 mills until the 20 mill level is reached. If approved by a three-fifths majority in both chambers of the legislature, the constitutional amendment would still require approval by voters.
Starkey has introduced the same bill five times previously without success. This year however, several key lawmakers have said they would support the measure.
They include House Speaker Jimmy Clark, D-Eufaula; and Senate Finance and Taxation and Education Committee Chairman Hank Sanders, D-Selma.
